translated_text: Liginiae, the 2nd, 01446 My darling, my Bobchen Lieber, my yout Finally I have received news that confirms my concern for your fate. I received the letter and his telegram from Perrigueux, but I didn't know you were in terrible conditions, heading towards a dreadful country. Your letter from Villeneuve-sur-Lot relieved me. If you weren't there, I wouldn't have known you would have spent a few days away from me—where you are. You are in France, where you are obviously being directed towards the Pyrenees. I don't mind finding you again, and then, provided that I can soon live a modest but bearable life with you, maintaining a happy game. I am asked if I wrote to your JP and also to Perrigueux, where unfortunately I couldn't telegraph; it was difficult. You must not have received my letters; I have a thousand and one things to say. I know where you went today; I simply want to write this little note to the towns you indicated. We are all still in Léginice, so rest assured, Alois, we haven't sworn off here, we've never moved. We intend to stay here for at least another two months. We are gradually settling in, and everything is going relatively well, so there's no reason to change places. Betty and Etienne will go to Paris later to see how things are going with our apartments. We will probably stay here – I myself am making various requests. Can you tell me what you want me to look for (to drive the car or wherever I go to where you are?). I think the Hérault is much better for us than the Corrèze (especially in winter if we are allowed to stay there or perhaps in Béziers). I'm waiting to be able to go to Masauté. Is Masauté well? I've just had a few horrible days, but not hearing from you is the most dreadful thing I know. It's worse than... I read my kind letter from Mrs. Blumenstein and U. Zentall. My Bobchen, I think of you all day. My only desire is to see you again very soon. I love you like crazy. "Son" Like a S to love your Babe. Зава LIGI POSTES REPUBLIQUE FRANÇAISE M.
